To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the excess entropy of fluids plays a key role in determining dynamical properties of fluids and that the excess entropy can be used to predict the relation of dynamically properties estimated from models of fluids at different resolution.

the excess entropy of fluids plays a decisive role in determining their dynamics and that the excess entropy of coarse grained models could play an equally decisive role in connecting dynamics of coarse grained and atomistic models of fluids.

(1) the dynamical speedup upon coarse graining of a molecular liquid can be estimated from the difference in excess entropies of the two systems; (2) the excess entropy of liquids is a function of temperature only; and (3) the excess entropy is the same for the same liquid at different pressures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theoretical framework for the description of the statistical mechanics of coarse grained models.
the statistical mechanics of coarse grained models.
the development of new methods for the simulation of complex molecular fluids and the development of new coarse-grained molecular dynamics methods to study complex fluids at the coarse-grained level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dynamical speedup upon coarse graining, which is a measure of the difference of the excess entropies of the atomistic and the coarse grained models, is given by the difference of the two entropies divided by the temperature.
the excess entropy is a fundamental measure for coarse graining and that its use in coarse-graining procedures is a necessary and sufficient condition for obtaining physically consistent results.

, for the system studied, the dynamical speedup is a function of the difference between excess entropies of the coarse grained and atomistic model, and the excess entropy is a function of temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamical speedups of coarse grained models can be estimated by measuring excess entropy differences.
the excess entropy of a fluid plays an important role in the determination not only of its equilibrium but of its dynamical properties as well.
the excess entropy is a useful quantity for understanding the dynamics of molecular systems, both in the atomistic and coarse-grained levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that

coarse graining of molecular systems is not a mere numerical trick to speed up simulations, but rather it can be seen as a way to explore the phase space of a given molecular fluid in a controlled manner, by changing the resolution at which we observe the system.
, in the absence of a microscopic theory, one can still make a quantitative prediction of the dynamical consequences of coarse graining by appealing to the notion of excess entropy.

the excess entropy of a coarse grained fluid is not only a good measure of the information loss incurred by the coarse graining, but it also provides an upper bound to the speedups achievable in molecular dynamics simulations of coarse grained fluids.
